questions.question: In chess, which piece is worth the least in terms of points?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**King**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The King is the most important piece in the game of chess, but in terms of points, it is typically considered to be worth the least.
 
• The king is the only piece that doesn't have a point value.
 
• The King can move one square in any direction (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally).
 
• If a player's King is checkmated, the game is over, and that player loses.
 
• Despite its low point value, protecting the King is crucial as losing the King results in losing the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Queen:**

 
 
• The Queen is the most powerful piece on the board and is worth 9 points.
 
• It can move any number of squares along a row, column, or diagonal.
 
 
 
• **Rook (Elephant):**
 
 
• The Rook is worth 5 points.
 
• It can move any number of squares along a row or column.
 
 
 
• **Knight (Horse):**
 
 
• The Knight is worth 3 points.
 
• It moves in an L-shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular to that.
 
• The Knight is the only piece that can 'jump' over other pieces.
 
 
 
• **Bishop:**
 
 
• The Bishop is also worth 3 points.
 
• It moves any number of squares diagonally.
 
 
 
• **Pawn:**
 
 
• The Pawn is worth 1 point, making it the least valuable piece in terms of points.
 
• It moves forward one square but captures diagonally.
 
• Pawns have the unique ability to be promoted to any other piece (except the King) if they reach the opponent's back rank.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Capital Expenditure?

I. Capital expenditure result in creation of physical or financial assets or reduction in financial liabilities.

II. Non-plan capital expenditure covers various general, social and economic services provided by the government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Capital expenditure** involves funds used by an entity to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets such as property, industrial buildings, or equipment.
 
• Capital expenditure results in the **creation of physical or financial assets** or reduction in financial liabilities.
 
• Non-plan capital expenditure covers various **general, social, and economic services** provided by the government.
 
• Both statements I and II accurately describe aspects of capital expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**

 
 
• It refers to funds used by an organization to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets such as buildings, machinery, or equipment.
 
• CapEx is often utilized for projects that are expected to produce benefits for more than one year.
 
• Examples include purchasing machinery, building a new factory, or upgrading existing facilities.
 
 
 
• **Non-plan Capital Expenditure**
 
 
• This type of expenditure is not part of the planned economic activities of the government but includes spending on general, social, and economic services.
 
• Examples include expenditure on defense equipment, public buildings, and infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Financial Assets**
 
 
• These are assets that derive value because of a contractual claim, such as bank deposits, bonds, and stocks.
 
• They are more liquid than physical assets and are often easier to trade.
 
 
 
• **Reduction in Financial Liabilities**
 
 
• This refers to the decrease in obligations that a company or government owes to external parties, including debt repayment.
 
• Reducing financial liabilities improves the financial health and creditworthiness of the entity.

questions.question: When a person seems to be working, but their work is not contributing to the output, it is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised unemployment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a person seems to be working, but their work is not contributing to the output, it is known as disguised unemployment. 
 
• Disguised unemployment is a type of unemployment where people are employed but their contribution to the total output is negligible.
 
• Even if some workers are removed, the output of the task remains unaffected.
 
• This often happens in agricultural sectors where family members work on a small plot of land, even though their contribution to the output is minimal.
 
• It's also known as hidden unemployment

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cyclical Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs due to fluctuations in the business cycle.
 
• During economic downturns, businesses reduce production and lay off workers, leading to a rise in unemployment.
 
• As the economy recovers, employment levels rise again.
 
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs when people are temporarily unemployed while transitioning between jobs.
 
• This can happen for various reasons, such as quitting a job voluntarily, getting layoffs, or searching for a job after completing education.
 
• It's considered a normal part of a healthy economy as people move between jobs to find better opportunities.
 
 
 
• Seasonal Unemployment:
 
 
• Occurs due to seasonal variations in demand for labor.
 
• Certain industries, like tourism, agriculture, and construction, experience fluctuations in demand throughout the year.
 
• As a result, workers in these industries may be unemployed during off-peak seasons.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that the State shall maintain just and honourable relations between nations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 51**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 51 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy and emphasizes promoting international peace and security.
 
• It states that the State shall maintain just and honorable relations between nations,
 
 
• foster respect for international law, and encourage the resolution of international disputes by arbitration.
 
 
 
• Article 51 outlines the following directives to the State to ensure peaceful coexistence and international cooperation:
 
• **Promote International Peace and Security**
 
 
• The State shall work to uphold global peace and security, which involves not only maintaining friendly relationships with other countries but also supporting actions that prevent conflicts and promote stability worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Maintain Just and Honorable Relations Between Nations**
 
 
• India aims to conduct its foreign affairs in a manner that respects sovereignty and fosters mutual respect. This principle advocates for fair and respectful relationships, aligning with the idea of global harmony.
 
 
 
• **Foster Respect for International Law and Treaty Obligations**
 
• The article encourages India to uphold international agreements and legal frameworks, signifying the importance of following global rules and regulations.
 
 
• This ensures that India respects the international community's established norms.
 
 
 
• **Encourage Settlement of International Disputes by Arbitration**
 
 
• By promoting peaceful resolution methods, like arbitration, India commits to resolving disputes diplomatically rather than through conflict. This reflects India's alignment with non-violence and peaceful negotiation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 47
 
 
• It mandates that the State should strive to improve the overall well-being of the people by focusing on nutrition, standard of living, and public health.
 
 
 
• Article 48
 
 
• It encourages the State to organize and improve agricultural practices and animal husbandry in a scientific manner.
 
 
 
• Article 49
 
 
• It directs the State to protect monuments, places, and objects of historic or artistic interest that are of national significance.

questions.question: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 by the Imperial Legislative Council.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was officially known as the “Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919”.
 
• Through this act, the British intended to replace the repressive provisions employed during wartime (Defence of India Act 1915) with a permanent one.
 
• The Act was passed by the Rowlatt Committee, presided by Sir Sydney Rowlatt. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was an indefinite extension of the Defence of India Act of 1915.
 
• The Imperial Legislative Council enacted it on 10th March 1919 to curb the upsurge of Indians against the Colonial rulers by depriving Indians of their right to liberty and expression.
 
• The act was prepared based on the recommendations put forth by the Rowlatt Commission of 1918.
 
• This act was called the Black Act by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The Rowlatt Act came to be repealed in 1922.

questions.question: Who of the following was invented and popularized Mohan Veena?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhat**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mohan Veena

 
 
• A Mohan Veena is one of two unique plucked string instruments used in Hindustani classical music, a genre of Indian classical music associated with the country's north.
 
• First, in 1948, Pandit Radhika Mohan Maitra created a musical instrument that combined the sarod, the veena, and the surbahar.
 
• In 1949, Thakur Jaidev Singh, the head producer of All India Radio at the time, gave the instrument the name "Mohan veena" in honour of Pt. Maitra.
 
• The Grammy Award-winning Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt invented and popularised the Mohan Veena, a Hawaiian guitar that has been modified.
 
• It is employed to perform classical Hindustani Ragas.
 
• Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Salil Bhatt (who later created the Satvik Veena, a variation of his father's Mohan Veena), and Canadian blues singer Harry Manx are a few of the well-known performers
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• This instrument, which has 20 strings in total, is actually a modified Archtop guitar.
 
• It has three to four melody strings, four to five drone strings strung from the peghead, and twelve sympathetic strings strung to tuners positioned on the side of the neck.
 
• To increase the sustain and resonance of the sound, a gourd (or Tumba) is put into the back of the neck.
 
• It is played with a bar and held in the lap similarly to a slide guitar.
 
• It is pulled by more than 500 pounds of strings together, which is a lot of tension. 
 
• The Chaturangui Veena, Hansa Veena, Shankar Veena, and many other famous variations of the Mohan Veena exist in India.

questions.question: What is the total rural literacy rate according to the 1951 census of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12.1 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The** total rural literacy rate** in India according to the 1951 census was **12.1 percent**.
 
• This rate reflects the percentage of the rural population that was literate at the time of the first census post-independence.
 
• The **1951 census **was the** first census** conducted in India after gaining independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• The literacy rate is a crucial indicator of educational development in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a **decennial exercise **conducted by the** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data about the demographic, social, and economic characteristics of the population.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, but the first complete census was conducted in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged seven years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• It is a key indicator of a country's educational development and human capital.
 
• Higher literacy rates are associated with better economic outcomes and improved quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Rural and Urban Classification**
 
 
• In the context of the Indian census, areas are classified as rural or urban based on certain criteria such as population density, percentage of male working population engaged in non-agricultural pursuits, and the presence of amenities like roads, electricity, and drinking water.
 
• Rural areas typically have lower population densities and fewer amenities compared to urban areas.

questions.question: In India, ________ is the legislative branch of governance; it is in charge of making laws.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Parliament**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legislative branch of governance in India is the Parliament of India, which is responsible for making laws
 
• The Parliament consists of the President and two houses: the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People
 
• The Parliament's basic function is to make laws. Legislative proposals are introduced as bills, which must be approved by both houses of Parliament and receive the assent of the President
 
• The Parliament is the supreme representative authority of the people and the highest legislative organ. It also exercises some control over the executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Supreme Court
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• Established in 1950, it has the power to interpret the Constitution, adjudicate disputes between states and the central government, and hear appeals against decisions from lower courts.
 
• The Supreme Court plays a crucial role in upholding the rule of law and safeguarding fundamental rights, often serving as a guardian of the Constitution. 
 
 
 
• President
 
 
• The President of India is the ceremonial head of state and the highest constitutional authority in the country.
 
• Elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories, the President's role is largely ceremonial, with real executive power vested in the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. 
 
 
 
• Home Minister
 
 
• The Home Minister of India is a key member of the Union Cabinet, responsible for internal security, law and order, and domestic affairs of the country.
 
• The Home Minister oversees the functioning of various departments, including police, intelligence agencies, and disaster management.
 
• This role is crucial for maintaining peace and stability within the nation, formulating policies related to internal security, and managing communal harmony.

questions.question: Which of the following is the unique dance tradition of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct option is__ Nati.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Nati dance is the most famous folk dance in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• A group of people performs it with accompanying musicians.
 
• Thora is the famous tribal dance of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The dress of the dance group reflects the gaddi or the Himachali

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bihu
 
 
• Bihu is a folk dance from the northeastern Indian state of Assam, celebrated during the Bihu festival,
 
 
• which marks the Assamese New Year and the onset of the harvest season.
 
• This energetic dance is characterized by lively movements, fast-paced rhythms, and traditional instruments like the dhol (drum) and Pepa (bamboo flute), symbolizing joy and gratitude for a bountiful harvest.
 
• Both men and women participate in Bihu, dressed in traditional attire, showcasing the vibrant culture and unity of the Assamese people.
 
 
 
 
 
• Cheraw
 
 
• Cheraw, also known as the Bamboo Dance, is a traditional dance of the Mizo people in the state of Mizoram.
 
• This dance is famous for its unique use of bamboo sticks, which are rhythmically clapped together on the ground as dancers step in and out of the gaps with grace and precision.
 
• The dance requires tremendous skill, coordination, and timing and is typically performed during festive occasions and important ceremonies, embodying the cultural richness and festive spirit of Mizoram.
 
 
 
• Dandari
 
 
• Dandari is a traditional folk dance from the tribal communities of Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh, performed during the Dussehra festival.
 
• This dance involves storytelling through music and movement, with dancers forming circles and using sticks (dandas) to create rhythmic beats.
 
• Dandari dancers represent mythological characters and narrate folk tales, symbolizing the connection between the communities and their cultural heritage, as well as celebrating communal harmony and the victory of good over evil.

questions.question: Which of these artists is a Manipuri dance style doyenne?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajkumar Singhajit Singh**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rajkumar Singhajit Singh is a highly respected artist and a doyenne of **Manipuri dance**,
 
• It is one of the classical dance forms of India originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• He is known for its graceful movements, intricate hand gestures, and unique rhythm,
 
• Manipuri dance is often associated with themes of devotion, particularly the tales of **Radha and Krishna**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gopi Krishan
 
 
• Gopi Krishan was an acclaimed Kathak dancer known for his innovation and charisma.
 
• He brought a unique style to Kathak, blending traditional movements with new elements that enhanced the appeal of the dance form.
 
 
 
• T Balasaraswati
 
 
• T Balasaraswati is celebrated as a leading Bharatanatyam dancer and was renowned for her intense expression and masterful control over the nuances of Bharatanatyam.
 
• Balasaraswati received prestigious honors, such as the **Padma Bhushan** and **Padma Vibhushan**, for her immense contributions to Bharatanatyam, preserving and promoting this dance form globally.
 
 
 
• Pt. Gopal Prasad Dubey
 
 
• Pt. Gopal Prasad Dubey is a master of Chhau dance, particularly the Seraikella Chhau style, which is known for its martial art-inspired movements and dramatic storytelling.

questions.question: In the Union Budget 2021-22, presented on 1st February 2021, the Finance Minister of India announced an outlay of INR 1.97 Lakh Crores for the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes for ________ key sectors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Union Budget 2022-23 Productivity Linked Incentive (PLI) sectors have increased to 14 sectors.
 
• The objective is to make domestic manufacturing globally competitive and to create global Champions in manufacturing.
 
• In the Union Budget 2021-22, presented on 1st February 2021, the Union Finance Minister announced an outlay of INR 1.97 Lakh Crores for the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes for 13 key sectors.
 
• This means that minimum production in India as a result of PLI Schemes is expected to be over US$ 500 billion in 5 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that the Productivity Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme in 14 sectors for achieving the vision of Atma Nirbhar Bharat has received an excellent response, with the potential to create 60 lakh new jobs, and an additional production of Rs. 30 lakh crore during next 5 years.
 
• The PLI Scheme for electronics manufacturing, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on 11 November 2020, has introduced the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme in 10 key sectors.
